summary: Inline review found that round 6 fixes the reported HTML discovery cases and removes automatic stale-lock recovery. Four material safety gaps remain: recursive ACL verification fails open, manual unlocks can break publish exclusion, ambiguous responses can clear pending protection, and explicit false flags authorize mutations. TypeScript validation passed; reproductions used offline Node mocks, with no live Instagram calls.

prior_blockers.title: HTML discovery can still continue after explicit account-stop signals
prior_blockers.evidence: HTML discovery now inspects challenge/login markers before HTTP failure classification (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/client.ts:254). Offline getPosts reproductions stopped at the discovery page for both the previously reported 403 challenge and 200 loginForm responses; read.ts:127 propagates those error kinds. Partial-data GraphQL account signals also stop at graphql.ts:143.

prior_blockers.title: Concurrent stale-lock recovery defeats publish exclusion
prior_blockers.evidence: Acquisition no longer automatically removes stale locks, and release checks its token (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/pending.ts:75, pending.ts:80, pending.ts:88). However, manual unlock still separates owner inspection from unconditional pathname removal (pending.ts:102, pending.ts:109). An offline overlapping-unlock reproduction allowed two publishes through the ledger check.

prior_blockers.title: Reused Windows Chrome profiles retain explicit permissions on descendants
prior_blockers.evidence: Authentication now requests recursive restriction before Chrome launches (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/auth.ts:240). Descendant reset and inspection exist, but reset failures and tree-scan exit status are ignored (secure.ts:85, secure.ts:99). An offline access-denied reproduction returned ok:true despite failed descendant isolation.

prior_blockers.title: Existing Windows cookie files receive credentials before their own permissions are secured
prior_blockers.evidence: Cookie replacement still exclusively creates an empty temporary file, restricts it before writing credential bytes, and renames it over the destination (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/cookie-store.ts:120, cookie-store.ts:126, cookie-store.ts:127, cookie-store.ts:128, cookie-store.ts:129).

prior_blockers.title: The previously reported transcode attempt-count discrepancy remains
prior_blockers.evidence: The bounded loop permits nine retries after the initial request (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:374, publish.ts:384). Offline execution counted exactly 10 configure requests for persistent video transcode_pending and one for photo transcode_pending.

strengths: Authenticated requests require HTTPS and an allowlisted Instagram hostname, with redirects disabled. Origin overrides remain restricted to Instagram; CDN bundle fetches supply no session cookies (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/client.ts:211, client.ts:233; constants.ts:27; graphql.ts:85).

Ordinary photo, carousel, story, edit-caption, delete, comment and reply dry runs made zero fetches in offline execution. Confirmed commands omitting experimental opt-in were rejected before client creation (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:124, main.ts:134, main.ts:139, main.ts:348, main.ts:352).

Routine authentication output is redacted: publish descriptions replace authentication headers, status displays cookie lengths, and GraphQL page tokens remain in memory (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:313; cookie-store.ts:177; main.ts:215; graphql.ts:65).

Generic 502 HTML and success without a media ID each produced one configure request, preserved unresolved state, and blocked the next publish in offline checks. Automatic configure retries are restricted to transcode_pending with video content (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:384, publish.ts:459, publish.ts:468).

Unreadable or corrupt pending state blocks publishing, and candidate matching never automatically resolves a record (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/pending.ts:118, pending.ts:128; publish.ts:408, publish.ts:440).

The CLI exposes no like, follow or DM commands, caps swipe research at 12 accounts and 50 posts per account, and defaults to 1.5-second pacing (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:301, main.ts:307; constants.ts:54; client.ts:108).
TypeScript validation passed with --noEmit across implementation and tests.

blocking_findings.title: Recursive Chrome-profile isolation still fails open
blocking_findings.why: Login can launch Chrome against a reused profile whose descendants were neither restricted nor successfully inspected, defeating the credential-storage contract.
blocking_findings.evidence: The recursive reset result is discarded. The subsequent tree scan checks only parsed output and ignores tree.ok; descendantsOnlyInherit accepts empty or error-only descendant output. With mocked access-denied failures for both recursive operations and a valid root ACL, restrictToCurrentUser returned ok:true. Authentication then proceeds to launch Chrome. Native ACL mutations were not exercised.

blocking_findings.title: Overlapping manual unlocks can delete an active publisher's lock
blocking_findings.why: The recovery command can admit overlapping publishes and bypass pending protection even though ordinary acquisition is now exclusive.
blocking_findings.evidence: unlockStale reads the owner, checks process liveness, then removes the pathname without checking that it still identifies that owner. Offline execution paused one unlock before removal, completed another unlock, and started publisher A. Resuming the first unlock deleted A's replacement lock. Publisher B then passed the ledger check while A was uploading. A subsequently became unresolved, but B still configured successfully: two configure calls without ignorePending or resolution.

blocking_findings.title: Non-JSON response classification permits unsafe fallback and clears ambiguous publishes
blocking_findings.why: Account-stop markers can be bypassed, and an ambiguous configure response can lose its pending record, allowing another publish despite uncertain server state.
blocking_findings.evidence: For JSON-expected requests, a non-JSON HTTP 404 becomes not_found before challenge/login inspection. An offline 404 challenge response therefore triggered the next authenticated candidate. Separately, HTTP 502 HTML containing challenge_required becomes checkpoint; executeLocked treats that kind as definitive and deletes the pending record despite the 5xx response. Two sequential offline publishes each reached configure after this response, with no pending record retained. These paths contradict the plan's promise that HTML and 5xx configure responses remain unresolved.

blocking_findings.title: Explicit false confirmation flags execute mutations
blocking_findings.why: A command explicitly setting confirmation and experimental opt-in to false can perform an unverified write instead of remaining a dry run or rejecting invalid syntax.
blocking_findings.evidence: parseArgs stores --confirm=false and --experimental=false as nonempty strings. Both gates test truthiness. Offline CLI execution of comment 123 --text x --confirm=false --experimental=false made one mutation fetch and emitted done:true using mocked storage and network.

open_questions: No live Instagram calls could be made. Payload acceptance, actual account-stop HTML, server-side transcode semantics and deletion behavior remain unverified; retaining experimental gates is necessary.

Bun was unavailable on PATH, and the full unit suite creates filesystem fixtures prohibited by this read-only environment. Runtime reproductions used Node TypeScript transformation and in-memory mocks.
Native Windows ACL mutation and Chrome profile reuse were not exercised. The recursive failure-handling defect was reproduced with mocked icacls results.

GraphQL response-root selection and pagination still lack demonstrated acceptance evidence. The live read test accepts an empty posts array and does not assert the reported source or pagination (instagram-ai-plugin/test/live.test.ts:36, live.test.ts:38).
